droppedAngles.why: Both new entry points (POST /withdrawals, GET /summary) reuse the exact same requireRole('admin', ...) wrapper as the existing /deposits route, which re-derives identity from the bearer token server-side (auth.js authenticate/requireRole), not from client input. withdraw() calls record(store, admin.id, 'withdrawal', accountId), attributing the action to the authenticated admin, identical in shape to deposit()'s existing record() call. Verified test 'a deposit raises...; a withdrawal lowers...' checks entriesFor(...).map(action) == ['account.open','deposit','withdrawal'], confirming attribution. No new trust boundary or identity-derivation path is introduced beyond the pattern already shipped for deposits.

droppedAngles.title: security
droppedAngles.why: No injection surface (no SQL/HTML/shell/URL construction from user input), no secrets or tokens added to code/logs (auth.js already forbids logging tokens and this diff doesn't touch that), no redirects, no CORS changes, no outbound third-party calls. The only new inputs (accountId, amountCents) go through the same store.get/Number.isInteger validation pattern as deposit's existing, unreviewed-as-new code path.

scoutNotes: Adds admin-only POST /withdrawals (the overdraw-refusing mirror of deposits) and admin-only GET /summary, which reads a per-currency running total from a new `totals` collection seeded by additive migration 003. The intent is that every deposit and withdrawal keeps `totals` current, but `withdraw()` never calls the `bumpTotal` helper that `deposit()` calls, so the running total only ever grows and is confirmed (by direct reproduction) to go stale/wrong after any withdrawal, while every added test stops short of re-checking `summary()` after a withdrawal.

confirmed.title: withdraw() never decrements the totals running balance
confirmed.rootCause: withdraw() in src/transfers.js debits the account's balanceCents but never calls bumpTotal(), so the totals collection backing GET /summary only ever increases from deposits and is never decremented by withdrawals.
confirmed.summary: withdraw() debits the account's balanceCents but never calls bumpTotal (or any totals update), so the new `totals` collection that GET /summary reads from only ever increases, even though real withdrawn money is supposed to be reflected.
confirmed.failure: Deposit 100 AUD into a fresh account, then withdraw 60 AUD. store.get('accounts', id).balanceCents correctly becomes 40, but summary(store) (and thus GET /summary for an admin) still reports { AUD: 100 }. I reproduced this directly: deposit(store, admin, {accountId, amountCents: 100}) followed by withdraw(store, admin, {accountId, amountCents: 60}) leaves summary(store) at { AUD: 100 } while the account balance is 40 — a 60-cent overstatement handed to the admin as 'money held per currency'. The divergence is permanent and compounds with every withdrawal thereafter (deposit() at line 62 calls bumpTotal(store, account.currency, amountCents); the symmetric call — bumpTotal(store, account.currency, -amountCents) — is simply absent from withdraw(), lines 68-80).

Ran the full existing test suite (`node --test`): all 24 tests pass on the unmodified PR head, confirming no existing test (including the new 'summary is for administrators and follows deposits' test, which only exercises a deposit then checks the account balance via GET /accounts, never re-checking GET /summary after the withdrawal) catches the gap. Both `totals` (schema addition), `bumpTotal`, `summary`, `withdraw`, and the `/withdrawals`/`/summary` routes are new in this diff, so the defect is correctly attributed as introduced by this diff. Severity CRITICAL is justified: GET /summary is the PR's headline deliverable and silently reports an inflated, permanently-diverging figure to admins as soon as a single withdrawal is made, directly contradicting the PR's own stated intent that totals are 'kept current' by every deposit and withdrawal.

confirmed.title: Withdraw's closed-account 409 path is never tested
confirmed.rootCause: No test in the PR calls withdraw() against a closed account, leaving the new 'a closed account cannot pay out' 409 branch completely unexercised.
confirmed.summary: withdraw()'s check order (closedAt before balanceCents<amountCents) is correct — verified by invariant and by a confirming test run against the PR's code — but no test in this diff ever calls withdraw() against a closed account, so the new 'a closed account cannot pay out' 409 branch is completely unexercised.
confirmed.failure: withdraw() in src/transfers.js:72-73 checks account.closedAt before the balance check, same order as deposit(). Since closeAccount() (src/accounts.js:45-46) refuses to close a non-zero-balance account, a closed account's balance is always 0, so for any positive amountCents a withdrawal against a closed account satisfies BOTH 409 conditions simultaneously. I confirmed by running a scratch test (openAccount -> closeAccount -> withdraw(1 cent)) against this worktree's code that it does throw 'cannot pay out' and never 'insufficient funds', so today's behavior is correct. But the only withdraw-specific test added in this diff (test/transfers.test.js, the test titled 'a deposit raises the currency's total; a withdrawal lowers the balance and never overdraws') exercises only the insufficient-funds path (amountCents=51 against a 50-cent open account) and the success path — it never opens-then-closes an account and calls withdraw() on it, and no other test (in test/server.test.js or elsewhere) does either. If a future edit swaps the two checks' order in withdraw(), or a future change to accounts.js lets a non-zero-balance account be closed (breaking the invariant this ordering silently depends on), a withdrawal against a closed account could start returning the wrong 409 message, or — if the balance check were dropped instead of reordered — could succeed in paying out of a closed account. No test anywhere in the suite would catch either regression, since nothing asserts which 409 fires when withdraw() is called against a closed account.

sites.title: Withdraw's closed-account 409 path is never tested

confirmed.reasoning: Verified every factual piece of this claim directly in the worktree. src/transfers.js:68-80 shows withdraw() checks `account.closedAt` (line 72, throws 409 'a closed account cannot pay out') strictly before `account.balanceCents < amountCents` (line 73, throws 409 'insufficient funds') — same order as deposit(). src/accounts.js:43-47 (closeAccount) confirms the invariant: it throws 'empty the account first' unless balanceCents === 0, so any closed account has balance 0, meaning for any valid positive amountCents both withdraw() guard conditions are true simultaneously and only check order decides the message. I wrote a scratch test (openAccount -> closeAccount -> withdraw(1 cent)) and ran it with `node --test`: it threw 'a closed account cannot pay out', confirming today's behavior and ordering are correct, exactly as the claim states. I then grepped every test file (test/transfers.test.js, test/server.test.js, test/accounts.test.js, test/store.test.js) for any call sequence that opens-then-closes an account and then calls withdraw() or POST /withdrawals on it — there is none. The only withdraw-specific test added by this diff (test/transfers.test.js:71-79, 'a deposit raises the currency's total; a withdrawal lowers the balance and never overdraws') only exercises insufficient-funds (amountCents=51 against a 50-cent balance) and the success path; the new server.test.js withdrawal call (line 88) is against an open, funded account. So the described gap is real and exactly as stated: a future reorder of the two checks, or a future removal of the balance check paired with a break of closeAccount's zero-balance invariant, would change withdraw()'s behavior against a closed account and no test in the suite would catch it. One nuance worth noting for calibration: this is a pre-existing pattern rather than something unique to withdraw() — deposit()'s own closed-account 409 ('a closed account cannot take a deposit', transfers.js:57) is likewise never asserted by any test in the repository, so the gap for withdraw() is this diff extending an existing untested-message pattern rather than a novel lapse. That nuance affects how surprising the finding is, not whether it is true, so I am not marking it refuted — all of the claim's factual and mechanistic assertions check out, and I could not refute the coverage gap. Given the real-world impact is modest (a check-order swap only changes which 409 message fires, since the invariant holds; only a compounding second regression — dropping the balance check entirely — would allow an actual overdraw), I'd rate this LOW rather than MEDIUM severity, but the finding itself stands.

missed.what: The PR's own docs/deploy.md states as an explicit, load-bearing invariant: 'Two copies can run against one file during a deploy.' Migration 003 adds a brand-new `totals` collection and bumps `version` to 3, but `Store` loads the whole file into memory once at process startup (src/server.js's `const store = await Store.open(file)`) and `save()` always serializes that entire in-memory snapshot (`JSON.stringify(this.data)`), never a partial/merged write (src/store.js). I verified with a standalone simulation (old pre-PR store.js vs. this PR's store.js against the same file) that if the pre-PR process is still running when the new release migrates and saves (adding `totals`, version 3), the OLD process's very next save -- triggered by something as ordinary as it handling one more deposit with code it already understood -- overwrites the file with its own stale in-memory data: `totals` disappears entirely (not merely stale, literally absent from the JSON) and `version` reverts to 2. Concretely: after the new process migrates, disk has `totals: [{id:'AUD',cents:500}], version:3`; after the old process's next unrelated save, disk has `totals: undefined, version: 2` and the old process's own stale balance silently replaces whatever the new process had written for that account. This is not the already-reported 'withdraw forgets to bump totals' bug -- it is the documented two-copy rollout window itself destroying the whole feature (and quietly reverting the schema version, which would cause migration 003 to simply re-run and rebuild totals from whatever balances happen to exist at that later moment, masking the loss).
missed.why: correctness and data-integrity review read transfers.js/migrations/003 as pure functions and checked their output against a single process's state; tests-that-dont-test and boundary-contract operate inside one Store instance in one test process, so they can never see a second stale Store instance clobbering disk; migrations-and-rollout, as run, evaluated migration 003 for being additive and matching existing balances at the moment it runs, not against docs/deploy.md's explicit 'two copies against one file' premise, which only bites when a second long-lived process's full-snapshot save happens after the first process's migration-triggered save -- a scenario no single-process test or code read would expose without actually running two Store instances against one file, which I did and confirmed produces exactly this data loss.
